title.zh: 轴对称磁通导出极向场

summary: Recover BR, BZ, and their magnitude from psi=R A_phi on a rectilinear cylindrical grid.

identity.relation: Axisymmetric field recovery from poloidal flux
identity.direction: R,Z,psi grids to BR, BZ, and B arrays
identity.definition: Differentiate psi on the rectilinear grid and divide by R, using the even-flux axis rule when R=0 is included.
identity.model: Stable local finite-difference gradients on a cylindrical R-Z grid.
identity.geometry: Two-dimensional rectilinear grid with increasing R and Z axes.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; psi Wb/rad; fields tesla.
identity.boundary: At R=0, BR is set to zero and BZ uses 2*(psi[:,1]-psi[:,0])/R[1]^2.
assumptions: All arrays are finite, matching, and at least 3 nodes per axis.
R and Z axes are strictly increasing.
psi is per-radian poloidal flux, not 2pi-linked flux.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.description: Cylindrical radius at each grid point.
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear grid with nonnegative, strictly increasing R axis and N_R >= 3; same shape as z_grid and psi.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.description: Axial coordinate at each grid point.
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear grid with strictly increasing Z axis and N_Z >= 3; same shape as r_grid and psi.

inputs.name: psi
inputs.description: Axisymmetric poloidal flux function R A_phi sampled on the R-Z grid, not full linked flux.
inputs.constraints: Finite values and exactly the same two-dimensional shape as the coordinate grids.

outputs.name: B_R
outputs.constraints: Zero at an included cylindrical-axis column.

outputs.name: B_Z
outputs.constraints: Uses the discrete axis rule if R=0 is included.

outputs.name: B
outputs.constraints: No fixed lower floor is applied.

preconditions: All arrays are finite, matching, and at least 3 nodes per axis.
R and Z axes are strictly increasing.
supported: Uniform and nonuniform rectilinear grids, axis regularization, rescaling, and finite large/subnormal values in direct tests.
excluded: Nonrectilinear grids, arbitrary extrapolation, and field-model validation beyond the tested finite differences.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for complex/nonfinite/mismatched arrays, nonrectilinear grids, too few nodes, or invalid axes.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Floating-point failures propagate if a finite accepted calculation is not representable.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; gradients and axis handling are direct.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No field mapping is returned after validation or arithmetic failure.

example.description: Recover the field from psi=R^2 on a grid including R=0.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import poloidal_field_from_flux
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.2, 0.4], [-0.5, 0.0, 0.5])
result = poloidal_field_from_flux(r_grid, z_grid, r_grid**2)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['B_R'], 0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['B_Z'], 2.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['B'], 2.0)
example.expected: B_R is zero everywhere and B_Z and B are 2 T everywhere, including the axis column.

scope: Quadratic-flux uniform-field and axis-rule regression on uniform and selected nonuniform grids.
A 2*pi rescaling of the psi input rescales the recovered axial field in a controlled quadratic example; full linked flux must be divided by 2*pi to recover psi=R A_phi.
Finite subnormal and large-magnitude hypot helper regression.
Constant psi=3.7 produces exactly zero field for three distinct grids.
A representable strong constant gauge on a manufactured even flux leaves BR/BZ invariant, including the axis.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Manufactured and analytic discrete checks establish only the stated poloidal model and declared integration geometry. Arbitrary Green matrices, pressure closures, experimental plasma applicability and public release are not established by these tests.
known_limitations: Caller-supplied physical closures and Green responses require their own evidence and coherent psi=R A_phi (Wb/rad) normalization.
Floating-point rounding envelopes do not bound discretization error or experimental uncertainty.
No expert scientific endorsement or public release follows from this numerical successor.
